Latest Update: Why Donald Trump Jr.’s investment firm is the focus of a widening probe in the House

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A top House Democrat is broadening his investigation into Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital fund 1789 Capital by demanding records from four companies that secured an investment before benefiting from lucrative federal contracts or policies.Rep.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A top House Democrat is broadening his investigation into Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital fund 1789 Capital by demanding records from four companies that secured an investment before benefiting from lucrative federal contracts or policies.Rep. Jamie Raskin, the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee and the panel’s incoming chair, sent letters on Monday evening to the defense contractor Hadrian Automation, vape maker Juul Labs, prediction market platform Polymarket and the online firearms seller GrabAGun.The Maryland congressman requested that each firm send him two years’ worth of communications with 1789 Capital and other select documents, saying the materials would help him investigate whether U.S. President Donald Trump’s eldest son used insider information to orchestrate or anticipate government actions that boosted the companies and his own finances. The investigation was opened over the summer Both Trump Jr. and 1789 Capital, which is based in Palm Beach, Florida, deny any wrongdoing.The letters ramp up an investigation that Raskin opened in August into Trump Jr.’s firm, which he said “suddenly struck investment gold” after naming the president’s son as a partner in 2024. As one of the lawmakers who will be spearheading Democrats’ oversight of the Trump administration when they take control of Congress in January, Raskin has said that uncovering information about bribery and financial corruption will be among his top priorities.Trump Jr. has repeatedly rejected accusations that he has exploited government access for profit. At an Axios event last week, he acknowledged that he understood people’s corruption concerns, but said that they weren’t accurate, noting he has been an investor for decades.“I can see what they are saying. It doesn’t make it so,” he said. “The notion that I should somehow sit in a corner, suck my thumb and wait, you know, eight years — in this case 12 years — till we’re out of the political game, it’s not real.” Trump Jr. and the firm deny any wrongdoing 1789 Capital also has forcefully denied claims of wrongdoing. In a letter to Raskin in September, the tech giant’s lawyers defended the firm’s investment thesis as predating Trump’s administration and said that while it “welcomes legitimate congressional oversight,” it “has no intention of being held hostage to political gamesmanship.”On Monday, the company’s attorney, Bill Burck, said the September letter explained flaws in Raskin’s understanding, but Raskin “never bothered to reply.”“Facts are facts and Congressman Raskin has them wrong here, but persists in his tall tales against 1789,” Burck said. “These are personal attacks untethered to actual evidence.” ‘Serendipitous timing’ of investments, Raskin states in letters The firm was founded in 2022 and Trump Jr. was announced as a partner in November 2024.In his letters to the four companies obtained by The Associated Press, Raskin outlined how federal policies or contracts had benefited their businesses and claimed that 1789 Capital had suspiciously “serendipitous timing” when it invested in them.Hadrian Automation, he wrote, received nearly $1 billion in U.S. Navy and Army contracts in March — its first-ever federal contracts — after bringing 1789 Capital on as an investor in 2025.Juul, Raskin wrote, received Food and Drug Administration clearance to keep its electronic cigarette products on the market in July 2025, four months after 1789 Capital had taken a stake in the company.The congressman wrote that GrabAGun got help from 1789 to go public and put Trump Jr. on its board before the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives issued a proposed rule to ease the process of shipping guns to people’s homes. Raskin calls Trump administration order ‘blatantly unlawful’ Raskin also raised questions about the Justice Department and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission closing investigations into Polymarket in July 2025, after 1789 Capital already had invested in the prediction market platform.GrabAGun said in a statement that Raskin’s letter “is a political document, and its allegations are baseless.”“ATF’s review of its regulations was well known across the firearms industry, and the agency published numerous proposed rules for public comment. GrabAGun’s only input came through public comments on several of those proposals,” the statement read.Juul Labs said that it was reviewing its letter closely.“As always, we intend to cooperate with any Congressional effort to understand our company, our commitment to combating underage vaping, and our mission to help adult smokers of combustible cigarettes transition completely away from smoking,” it said in an emailed response.The other recipients of the letters didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.The Trump administration has taken steps to push back on the Democrats’ oversight efforts, including an executive order on Friday directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged.That could complicate compliance with Raskin’s investigation for at least one of the companies, Hadrian Automation, which is a federal contractor.Raskin has called Trump’s order “blatantly unlawful” and said that public contractors have a “duty and a right to speak truthfully when Congress calls.” —Ali Swenson, Associated Press.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that following the news that Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has returned to the company as CEO a little more than a week after he resigned from the role, it's now believed that he admitted to additional extra-marital affairs beyond the two that were already known.
  • The report details a November 22 meeting in which Huang and the Nvidia board sat down to discuss his return.
  • The company remarked its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that following the news that Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has returned to the company as CEO a little more than a week after he resigned from the role, it's now believed that he admitted to additional extra-marital affairs beyond the two that were already known. The admission came during an hours-long meeting with Huang as Nvidia's board members discussed him potentially coming back to a company he left in disarray when he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The woman, Alice Huang, worked for Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer that is now under criminal investigation over its possible involvement in the smuggling of export-controlled Nvidia AI chips into China. Now, with Huang back in the top job at Nvidia, a WSJ report claims that the company's board rehired him despite the revelation that his affairs outnumbered the two already reported.

The report details a November 22 meeting in which Huang and the Nvidia board sat down to discuss his return. Huang told the board that there were more affairs than those it already knew about, with people with knowledge of the discussions saying that he was contrite about his behavior. Then, after the board explained to Huang that it was notable that he be honest and candid after at least one affair with an Nvidia employee, it was agreed that the best thing for the company would be for Huang to return. Huang has confessed to being unfaithful to his wife, Lori, reportedly carrying on an affair with Megaspeed's Alice Huang and Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. The report explicitly states Huang admitted to multiple further affairs, bringing the total of known instances to at least four.

The company remarked its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang. It's unclear whether its decision was affected by Nvidia's 24% stock price fall following Huang's affair scandal first broke. President Trump also stated he heavily lobbied for Huang's return, personally dialling in to an Nvidia board meeting to persuade the company to reinstate him.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this,” Huang reportedly remarked in a video of his return to the Nvidia offices. “I’ve made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back.”.

Sources indicate that huang's return to Nvidia came after a week of uncertainty for the manufacturer. Calls for his return were made by everyone from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to U.S. President Trump. The latter was very vocal in his stance on Huang and has since taken the credit for Nvidia's decision to reinstate him. This came after he initially called for former Apple CEO Tim Cook to take the reins of the company.

According to recent reports, one of Huang's first acts as the returning Nvidia CEO will be to appear before a House Foreign Affairs panel. He'll do so on December 1 to answer questions about his affair with Alice Huang in the context of import-controlled AI chips finding their way into China.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dunkin’ is celebrating the holiday season with the return of its free donut giveaway, a giant nutcracker statue, and a limited-edition merchandise collection.
  • The coffee chain introduced its Donutcracker character as part of its 2026 holiday packaging, featuring the festive design on cups, donut boxes, and Munchkins boxes.
  • Now, starting on Black Friday, November 27, Dunkin’ is bringing the character to life for the first time alongside a series of holiday promotions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dunkin’ is celebrating the holiday season with the return of its free donut giveaway, a giant nutcracker statue, and a limited-edition merchandise collection.

The coffee chain introduced its Donutcracker character as part of its 2026 holiday packaging, featuring the festive design on cups, donut boxes, and Munchkins boxes.

Now, starting on Black Friday, November 27, Dunkin’ is bringing the character to life for the first time alongside a series of holiday promotions.

Dunkin’ is installing a 15-foot-tall Donutcracker statue at Historic Fort Steuben’s Christmas at the Fort celebration in Steubenville, Ohio.

The city is home to the world’s largest collection of life-size nutcrackers, with the Dunkin’ character set to join more than 200 others at the holiday attraction.

Visitors can also purchase exclusive Donutcracker merchandise at the Dunkin’ restaurant at 1987 Sunset Boulevard in Steubenville while supplies last.

A separate limited-edition merchandise collection will launch on November 27 at noon ET, featuring three items:.

Additional holiday collectibles, including tumblers, ornaments, and mugs, will arrive at participating restaurants nationwide in early December, with prices ranging from $12.99 to $34.99.

Alongside the Donutcracker’s debut, Dunkin’ is bringing back its Free Donut Fridays promotion for three consecutive weeks.

Dunkin’ Rewards members can claim a free Classic Donut with any qualifying beverage purchase on November 27, December 4, and December 11 at participating US locations.

Customers can redeem the offer by ordering through the Dunkin’ app, scanning their Rewards ID at checkout, or paying with an enrolled Dunkin’ card.

According to recent reports, the promotion is limited to one free donut per member each Friday and excludes specialty donuts. Both the beverage and donut must be included in the same order, and the offer cannot be combined with other promotions or Meal Deals.

Dunkin’s viral 48oz bucket drinks return with special cup holder to fit in cars.

Dunkin assembles Avengers: Doomsday menu featuring Doctor Doom and X-Men.

Dunkin’ is opening a drive-thru for dogs with treats, toys and exclusive merch.

#116517. Google broke its biggest promise about Gmail. It’s the one thing no manufacturer should ever do

Google broke its biggest promise about Gmail. It’s the one thing no manufacturer should ever do

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, promises, by their very nature, are inconvenient.
  • Promises, by their very nature, are inconvenient.
  • Recent findings suggest that of course, the benefit of all that inconvenience is that people trust you when you keep your promises.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, promises, by their very nature, are inconvenient. You tell someone you’re going to do something, and then you have to do it. Or, you promise you’ll never do something, and now you’ve restricted your options. Of course, the benefit of all that inconvenience is that people trust you when you keep your promises. And trust, as I’ve written before, is your most valuable asset, especially when you’re a massive tech giant whose entire business depends on the willingness of your customers to give you their personal information. Like Google. Which is why it was such a significant deal back in 2017 when Google promised it would not scan your Gmail in order to show you personalized ads. Previously, Google would scan your email to decide which ads to show. People didn’t love that, so Google told customers their data was their own and wouldn’t be used for ads. For almost a decade, that was the deal. You could use Gmail, Google Photos, and Google Drive without worrying that the information you stored in those services would be used as a source of ad recommendations. Earlier this month, however, the company quietly updated its privacy policy to say that it would use information from Gmail, Google Photos, and Google Drive to influence the ads people see. Specifically, the policy—which took effect October 16—claims that information from those services can be used to personalize advertisements when users choose to connect them to other Google products that have personalized advertising. The most obvious reason Google is doing this is Personal Intelligence, which lets users connect their Gmail, Search, and Photos to Gemini. The reason you might want to do this is that it turns out that AI can be very useful at pulling information from your email, for example. Of course, that’s very different from wanting Google to then show you ads based on what it finds. To be clear, it’s not that Google is suddenly scanning everyone’s inbox to sell ads. You have to turn on the connection—it’s off by default. In addition, Google isn’t giving your personal information to advertisers, and it says it doesn’t directly target ads based on the data you have in those services. Instead, Google’s AI can use information derived from connected apps to personalize ads. I’m sure there’s some kind of technical distinction there, but I don’t know that it’s all that meaningful if you’re someone who has trusted Google with all your information. Say, for example, you are planning a trip, and you ask Gemini to help you plan activities when you’re there. You give it access to your email so it can find your flights and then track whether the price changes. That’s super useful, and it’s the kind of thing that AI tools are actually really good at. Imagine, however, if suddenly you started seeing ads for things to do near your travel destination. Under Google’s latest policy, information derived from that reservation could definitely influence the advertisements you see. Look, it’s not that Google is doing something inherently wrong. You can certainly decide for yourself whether you want to connect your accounts at all. Also, to its credit, Google is disclosing how that information might be used. The problem is that Google is changing the terms of a promise it made in order to earn people’s trust in the first place. And you can’t connect Personal Intelligence and take advantage of its genuine benefits without opting in to the ad part. Every company eventually faces a situation where keeping a promise it made to its users suddenly becomes inconvenient. Maybe it’s because the market changes, or because its competitors introduce something new, or there’s an opportunity to make more money. When that happens, it’s tempting to find a technical reason for changing the terms of the deal. Google could reasonably argue that its new policy is different from its old practice because users have to opt in and their emails aren’t directly used to select advertisements. But you don’t build trust with technical distinctions in your privacy policy. You build it by being clear about what customers can expect, and then doing exactly that. In Google’s case, the promise was simple: We won’t use the information you put in Gmail to personalize advertising. Now, if you want to connect your personal information to Google’s AI product, it will. The most important thing a company can do is keep its promises, especially when doing so becomes inconvenient. The worst thing that can happen is that customers start wondering which promises you’ll keep and which ones you’ll change when you see a better business opportunity. Once that happens, you’ve already lost something far more valuable than whatever you hoped to gain. —Jason Aten This article originally appeared on Fast Company’s sister website, Inc.com. Recent findings suggest that elementor made your site easy to build. It may also be making it slow. Here's how to move a site onto the Block Editor without breaking URLs, losing content or dropping out of Google.

Page builders solved a real problem. Before the Block Editor matured, they were the easiest way to give clients drag-and-drop layouts. Many of those sites are still running today, and a lot of them are slow on phones.

The data backs that up. According to the HTTP Archive Core Web Vitals Technology Report for June 2026, 36.8% of Elementor sites pass Core Web Vitals on mobile. Sites built with the Block Editor pass 53.0% of the time. That's correlation, not proof, since hosting and setup matter too. But in my experience, it matches what happens when you remove the builder from a slow site.

My reason for migrating sites off Elementor is simple: **page builders make websites heavy. **Having said that, Elementor has improved a lot. Its performance settings, Flexbox Containers, and asset-loading options cut much of the bloat, and a carefully tuned Elementor site can pass Core Web Vitals. But tuning only goes so far. You’re still shipping the builder’s framework, wrapper markup and scripts, and every plugin or Elementor update is a chance for the speed to slip again.

For small business sites that don’t need drag-and-drop editing, rebuilding the same design on the WordPress Block Editor (Gutenberg) removes that weight at the source, without changing what the client sees.

Recent findings suggest that this guide follows the order I use. It assumes you're comfortable with WordPress admin, WP-CLI and a staging site. If you need to set those up first, SitePoint's guide to the ultimate WordPress development environment covers the tooling.

Not every Elementor site needs to move. Migration makes sense when:.

It's harder to justify when the site leans on Elementor Pro features you'd need to replace, such as complex popups, dynamic loops or WooCommerce templates. Those can all be rebuilt, but the job gets bigger fast.

You can't prove a migration worked without "before" numbers. Capture these on the live site first.

Recent findings suggest that crawl the site with a tool such as Screaming Frog, and export every indexable URL with its title, meta description, H1 and canonical tag. You can also pull published pages and posts with WP-CLI:.

Industry observers note that run Google PageSpeed Insights, which uses Lighthouse for its lab scores, on the homepage and two or three key templates. Save the mobile lab scores and, if the site has enough traffic, the field data from real customers.

According to recent reports, export the last three months of pages and queries from Google Search Console. That's what you'll compare against after launch.

Elementor stores each page's layout as JSON in the elementordata post meta field, and marks builder pages with elementoredit_mode. This command lists every page that uses the builder:.

Then list everything else Elementor controls, which is easy to miss:.

Industry observers note that on the small business sites I've migrated, the inventory usually turns up more than the owner expects. The pages are the easy part. The surprises are saved templates nobody remembers creating, a popup still running on every page, add-on widgets from plugins that were installed once and forgotten, and contact forms that live inside Elementor Pro rather than a form plugin. Finding those before the rebuild saves a broken launch.

Work on a staging copy. Install a block theme, such as Twenty Twenty-Five or a lightweight starter theme, and move the Elementor global styles into theme.json. That way colors, fonts and spacing are defined once, instead of in every widget.

It has been revealed that copy the hex values and font names from Elementor's Site Settings so the upcoming site matches the old one. Rebuild the header and footer as template parts in the Site Editor. If you'd rather write a theme yourself, SitePoint's series on building a WordPress theme from scratch covers the basics.

Most Elementor sites repeat the same few sections: a hero, a services grid, testimonials and a call to action. Build each one once as a block pattern, then reuse it on every page. Patterns are plain block markup, so you don't need React to write them, whatever you may have heard about React and WordPress development.

In a block theme, any PHP file in the /patterns folder with a header comment is registered automatically:.

For page content, there's a useful shortcut. Elementor saves a plain HTML copy of each page into post_content. Open a page in the Block Editor, and the old content usually appears in a Classic block. Choose Convert to blocks, then delete the leftovers and rebuild the layout with your patterns. It keeps the copy and images, so you only redo the design.

The difference shows up in the page source. Here's typical front-end markup for a single heading on an Elementor page, using the older section and column layout:.

And the same heading as a block:.

Newer Elementor versions with Flexbox containers and the optimized markup settings trim some of those wrappers, but most older sites still carry all of them. Multiply that by every element on every page, and the weight adds up.

To speed up this step, I built a free Elementor to Gutenberg converter. Paste in a page's elementordata JSON from Step 2, and it returns block markup you can paste into the Block Editor's code editor. It handles headings, text, images, buttons, spacers, dividers and column layouts, and lists anything it can't convert, such as forms and popups, for you to rebuild by hand. It runs entirely in your browser, so the page data never leaves your computer.

The code is rarely what holds a migration up. Content is. Once clients see their site being rebuilt, many decide it's time to rewrite their pages too, and the project ends up waiting on copywriters and approvals. My fix is to separate the two: migrate the existing content as it is, launch, then revision the copy afterwards. That keeps the speed and SEO gains on schedule, and it means any ranking change can be traced to either the migration or the fresh copy, not both at once.

This is the step that decides whether rankings hold.

To spot-check a redirect or a status code from the command line:.

When staging matches the live site, deploy it. Then:.

Leave the old elementordata meta in place for a few weeks, in case you need to roll back. Once you're confident, take a backup and remove it to shrink the database.

Run PageSpeed Insights again straight away for lab scores. Field data takes longer: the Chrome UX Report uses a rolling 28-day window, so give it a month before judging real-user results. Compare Search Console clicks for the same period before and after launch.

Industry observers note that in my migrations, the biggest change is usually page weight and loading time, because the builder's CSS, JavaScript and wrapper markup are gone. What doesn't always improve is server response time. If the site is on slow shared hosting, the first byte still arrives late, and that needs a hosting fix, not a rebuild. Search traffic should hold steady if the URLs and metadata were protected. If it drops, the Step 5 crawl comparison is the first place to look.

According to recent reports, moving off Elementor isn't a one-click job, but it isn't a full redesign either. Record a baseline, inventory what the builder controls, rebuild with patterns, and protect every URL. Most of the speed gain comes from removing code the site never needed. For what to tackle after that, see these practical web performance techniques. Most of the risk comes from rushing the SEO checks. Done carefully, the client gets the same site, a faster one, and an editor that comes with WordPress itself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide. It's destined to become the largest video game release of all time, and probably one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. So we're doing a launch day live blog to chart its arrival in the world.

Have you played it yet? I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go. I couldn't manage it but my college-age son was contemplating it. And if you have played it, what do you think - what are your early impressions? Is this what you were waiting for?

In a recent development, more broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world. I've already seen nearly all mainstream news and media outlets attempt to cover the game - and many other kinds of businesses - so will GTA 6 make people reappraise video games?

Moreover, exactly how substantial will the launch be? The record books are ready to be written in, but what exactly will be written? And how will other games fare in GTA's wake - better, or worse? There's lots to consider as the ripples spread around the world.

It has been revealed that we'll pull-in stories and developments, and your comments, as we chart the arrival of Rockstar's game around the world. Let's get to it.

Our live coverage of this event has finished.

Recent findings suggest that an historic day in gaming and there's loads to unpack. But to begin with, this: did you take a day off to play GTA 6, and have you played it yet?

Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

Sources indicate that the marketing push by Rockstar to have GTA 6 imprint on real-world cities has been impressive to see. There have been festivals in Miami, Selfridges dedicated a portion of its department store to selling GTA merch, but there's more than this besides. The London Standard summarised much of the activity in London in a video on Instagram.

A post shared by The Standard (@thelondonstandard).

Rockstar employment tribunal verdict could take weeks.

Sources indicate that the din of release is in danger of drowning out the Rockstar employment tribunal that came to a close this week in Scotland. Former Eurogamer video producer Chris Bratt - now co-owner of People Make Games - has been following the case closely, and reported yesterday that a verdict in the case could take "weeks".

He quotes Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as promptly as I possibly can.".

In a recent development, and that's it for the Rockstar tribunal! We await the judge's decision, but how long will it take? Judge Lucy Wiseman: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Yesterday, we independently confirmed that most, if not all, of the fired Rockstar employees are credited in the GTA 6 credits - which are, according to Chris Tapsell, our reviewer, an enormous thing in their own right.

Here’s how big it is, news-wise:.

Yesterday, my mother _(whose single dabble in gaming over the years can be described as,“working out the way to bypass the Brontosaurus Guarding Causeway in the text adventure Time Machine, is to GIVE it the Ship’s Biscuit found aboard the Marie Celeste”)_ texted me to ask if I was “ready for tomorrow?”.

I instantly assumed I’d made or hinted at some initiative to do something with her and subsequently forgotten.

Recent findings suggest that BUT, NO. She was asking if I was ready for GTA. A product I have never mentioned in her presence in all my many years.

So if you’ve got the over-seventies non-gamers talking… I’d say you’ve cracked it.

Recent findings suggest that goodness! And will your mother also be playing it?

My inbox is flooded with all kinds of brands trying to get in on the GTA 6 hype.

Recent findings suggest that the most recent one? Petrol prices. "Having to refuel your car in GTA 6 adds another layer of realism to the game, but it's something real-life drivers have to think about every time they get behind the wheel," stated Beth Fountain, fuel expert at somewhere called Interfuels.

"With petrol and diesel prices remaining high, filling up can take a significant chunk out of someone's monthly budget, particularly for those who rely on their vehicles for work or regular travel.

"While players might find the newly introduced mechanic frustrating, it's a reminder of how much we depend on fuel in everyday life and how rapidly those costs can add up.".

There's another one from Just Eat, the food delivery company, which has apparently made a real controller with Just Eat order button on it for you to order food while gaming. It's not specifically GTA 6-linked but it's jumping on that bandwagon. The controller is apparently synced to your Just Eat account. Imagine mashing that by accident and having an accidental feast turn up.

"When you're deep into a high-stakes gaming session nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food. With the Just ChEAT Button, Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play," stated Just East UK and Ireland marketing director Tina Koehler.

It's not clear where you can buy this controller or how much it costs. It's described as "limited edition". I wonder if that means only one has been made.

The goofy things people are already doing in GTA 6.

Many people are playing GTA 6 already of course and doing expectedly bizarre things in it. From lobbing hammers like Crocodile Dundee lobs cans of tinned food, to dropkicking people, to attempting to dive through a car window while oiled up and in one's pants - Connor has rounded up some of the goofiest clips around.

You are brilliant, Eurogamer readers!

I just want to resurface the winning entry to the GTA memories competition we ran at the tail-end of last week, because it's funny and uplifting, and I still smile about it.

My favourite GTA memory is introducing my nan to Vice City.

She'd never played a video game before, so I told her she could pretty much do whatever she wanted.

She spent the first 20 minutes driving around obeying traffic lights and apologising whenever she bumped into another car.

Then she accidentally punched someone.

I don't know what happened, but something just clicked.

Within half an hour she'd stolen a police car, run over several pedestrians and was shouting at the telly because the police wouldn’t leave her alone.

My grandad came in to see what all the noise was about.

Without even looking up she just said, "I'm wanted for murder, Barry. Put the kettle on.".

Genuinely one of the funniest afternoons of my childhood.

I'm on the management team for a charity and they've scheduled their AGM for tonight at 6pm. Of all the dates! I've had to weigh up not doing my duty for selfish video game reasons.

According to recent reports, "We're seeing a significant increase in interest in the PS5 Pro, with demand jumping by 57 percent in the week leading up to launch. At the same time, the price of the console has climbed by more than £450 since the end of October.".

GTA 6 is Metacritic's highest rated game ever.

More ridiculous GTA 6 launch piggybacking and this time it's an email with a therapist talking about how the game might help teens with their dating outlooks.

Says Natalie Buchwald, therapist and founder of Manhattan Mental Health Counseling:.

"Psychologists sometimes talk about 'relationship scripts': the unspoken expectations we absorb about how relationships work, what partners owe each other and what success looks like. We pick these up long before we have much experience of our own, from family, friends, online spaces and the stories we see in entertainment.

"No single film, game or influencer shapes someone's values on its own. What matters more is the overall mix of messages a person encounters, and whether they have the space to question them. That's particularly relevant now that dating advice is so widely available online, where some content frames relationships around status, control or getting something in return, rather than mutual respect.

It has been revealed that "That's why the most useful thing parents can do isn't to hand over a set of rules. It's to help young people think critically about the scripts they're picking up. Being curious rather than critical, and asking what they've seen, what they think of it and what they believe makes a good partner, tends to keep conversations open.

Industry observers note that "Entertainment can play a helpful role here. A story built around a partnership, like Jason and Lucia's, can give parents a natural, low pressure starting point for conversations that might otherwise feel awkward.".

According to recent reports, chris referenced some of this in his review, praising Jason's tender and caring side, and his not being a toxic asshole. GTA 6 is also the first game to not only feature a couple but a female playable lead, having very much revolved around male fantasies in the past.

Leaders: transformation should not be your focus

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1349 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In his 1980 book Managing in Turbulent Times, management guru Peter Drucker wrote, “The greatest danger in times of turbulence is not the turbulence; it is to act with yesterday’s logic.” This seems obvious.
  • Recent findings suggest that in his 1980 book Managing in Turbulent Times, management guru Peter Drucker wrote, “The greatest danger in times of turbulence is not the turbulence; it is to act with yesterday’s logic.” This seems obvious.
  • It may be tempting to think that the other side of turbulence is overhauling the organization in a major transformation effort.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In his 1980 book Managing in Turbulent Times, management guru Peter Drucker wrote, “The greatest danger in times of turbulence is not the turbulence; it is to act with yesterday’s logic.” This seems obvious. But more often than not, businesses lean into safe, tried and true, old-school thinking as their life raft during uncertain times. Consider Nvidia, initially defending keeping Jensen Huang in place as CEO amidst accusations of major ethical missteps. It may be tempting to think that the other side of turbulence is overhauling the organization in a major transformation effort. But Geoff Tuff and Steve Goldbach, who are leaders in Deloitte’s sustainability practice, have a different take on moving through organizational turbulence. They believe that large-scale transformation is not the right focus. In fact, their research and experience show that organizations who focus on transformation tend to fail. What they offer instead is an alternative view that is compellingly explored in their book Hone: How Purposeful Leaders Defy Drift. Cumulatively, Geoff and Steve have decades of experience working with Fortune 500 companies that end up drifting in the process of trying to transform. When I recently spoke with them they shared that “drift” is the unintentional, imperceptible shift that leaves an organization uncompetitive because leaders fail to make micro-adjustments along the way. The solution? Hone: make small, intentional continuous adjustments to stay on course rather than wait until a massive disruption is necessary. Here are my three biggest takeaways from our conversation. 1. Honing is the antidote to failed transformation. Broad-scale transformations carry a 70% failure rate because humans naturally resist drastic change. This leads to organizational “tissue rejection.” Instead replace massive transformation with continuous “honing” to prevent drift. Geoff’s pastime and love of sailing have clearly influenced their perspective. Because just like adjusting a boat’s autopilot to account for winds and currents, leaders should focus on honing (for example, micro-adjustments in leadership style, accountability, KPI’s, etc.)  to stay on course rather than wait until a massive, disruptive transformation is required. 2. AI can help identify where honing is needed. Invisible drift can be made visible because AI can detect subtle patterns and organizational drift that are otherwise invisible to the human eye, enabling managers to address problems proactively. An AI enabled organizational network analysis can track thousands of interactions over time (such as email and Slack messages about meetings). For example, it can spot if an engineering team’s contact with the product team has decreased over 30% over multiple quarters. A 2021 study published in Nature Human Behaviour showed that a 60,000 person Microsoft team’s collaboration efforts decreased when the team went remote. Employees engaged in more intra-team communication than inter-team communication. AI can serve as an early warning system, surface weak signals and alert leaders about a future they may not want so that they can course correct. 3. Honing demands deep behavioral curiosity. The good news is that we can adopt a “honing mindset.” A successful “honer” walks through the world constructively dissatisfied with current processes. And not because they’re unhappy, but because they’re more critically curious and attuned to identify design flaws, eliminate waste, and continuously tweak systems. Organizations change when the individuals within them start behaving differently. To drive that change, leaders must practice self-awareness and empathy to understand what truly motivates their teams. If you’re wondering how to make honing a regular behavioral practice on your own team, start by inviting someone in from the outside. It should be a person from a different team or even a different industry who can cast a bird’s eye view on your operations and ask the “naive questions.” In design thinking we call this “lateral thinking.” Then, collect three of their questions and keep them as regular trackers that you continuously go back to asking yourself and your team as navigational tools. Because just as it’s easier to spot a ship that’s going off course from the shoreline, an outsider can help spark the necessary micro-adjustments to ensure that you’re honing- not drifting.

Recent findings suggest that in his 1980 book Managing in Turbulent Times, management guru Peter Drucker wrote, “The greatest danger in times of turbulence is not the turbulence; it is to act with yesterday’s logic.” This seems obvious. But more often than not, businesses lean into safe, tried and true, old-school thinking as their life raft during uncertain times. Consider Nvidia, initially defending keeping Jensen Huang in place as CEO amidst accusations of major ethical missteps.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that project Leonida, a recompilation project aiming to bring the console version of GTA 6 to the PC, has been shut down, with its Discord and GitHub servers taken offline.
  • The project to make GTA 6 run on a Windows PC months ahead of the game's expected early 2027 release window is one of a run of similar recompilations, some of which have proven successful.
  • Industry observers note that in the case of this ill-fated project, it came just days after notorious leaker Cyberleek made a near-complete build of the Xbox version of GTA 6 available online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that project Leonida, a recompilation project aiming to bring the console version of GTA 6 to the PC, has been shut down, with its Discord and GitHub servers taken offline. The 15-year-old kid behind the project has admitted that Rockstar took down the server, adding that the life of a teenager is hard enough "without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." The Project Leonida Discord server had almost 180,000 members when it was taken offline, TechPowerUp reports. NotRezed, the account behind the project and associated online presences, has also confirmed that they have been banned from Discord for two years.

The project to make GTA 6 run on a Windows PC months ahead of the game's expected early 2027 release window is one of a run of similar recompilations, some of which have proven successful. Earlier this year, we saw Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought to Apple platforms, months before the game's remake was declared for the Nintendo Switch 2. That same game is now circulating online after an AI-assisted jailbreak allowed it to be dumped immediately following its release. Similar AI assistance has helped the recompilation efforts of multiple projects in recent months, and GTA 6 is unlikely to be the last.

https://t.co/brVVmcwx9dNovember 23, 2026.

Industry observers note that in the case of this ill-fated project, it came just days after notorious leaker Cyberleek made a near-complete build of the Xbox version of GTA 6 available online. A missing executable for the game was then also released on November 23, with recompilation efforts taking note. And while Project Leonida is no more, there's no indication that other parallel projects will follow suit.

As for NotRexed, they say that they "really want to make cool stuff," but that things have happened that they "can't control," and they will be stepping away as a result.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 was released on the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S platforms on November 19 and immediately shot to the top of sales charts. It's since been confirmed that the game reached $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales with 32.5 million units sold pre-release. Sony has also confirmed that the game set a newly introduced record for the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation, with players logging 683 million hours of gameplay by November 23. The game has captured the attention of gamers everywhere, with one even using mind control and eye tracking to hijack an in-game airplane.

Breaking: AI upended entry-level jobs. Here’s what employers are actually looking for

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI is changing nearly every aspect of the workplace—but especially entry-level jobs, to the point where Gen Z is calling for millennials (who are only in their 30s and 40s) to retire to make room.
  • AI is changing nearly every aspect of the workplace—but especially entry-level jobs, to the point where Gen Z is calling for millennials (who are only in their 30s and 40s) to retire to make room.
  • A recent survey of nearly 7,000 workers, managers, and executives found that 51% believe AI is reducing early-career opportunities, while 49% say tasks that traditionally helped employees build work experience are increasingly being handled by AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI is changing nearly every aspect of the workplace—but especially entry-level jobs, to the point where Gen Z is calling for millennials (who are only in their 30s and 40s) to retire to make room. Many are placing the blame on AI for making tasks in many entry-level jobs outdated; data seems to back that up. A recent survey of nearly 7,000 workers, managers, and executives found that 51% believe AI is reducing early-career opportunities, while 49% say tasks that traditionally helped employees build work experience are increasingly being handled by AI. Another shows that entry-level listings have plummeted 35% since 2023; another suggests entry-level jobs in Newly introduced York City have been cut in half. That means the pressure is on for early-career candidates to show employers what they can bring to a role beyond their ability to use AI tools. A catch-22 emerges: many employers increasingly turn to AI, yet many also want candidates who can think independently, come up with original ideas, recognize when to put the technology aside and trust their own judgment. Indeed, many young workers find themselves in a tricky-to-navigate, even unfair entry-level job market. Luckily, there are tips that can make you stand out in a labor market that both increasingly relies on AI, and that also demands workers show employers the human skills they’re looking for. Don’t let AI write your resume for you Sure, AI can be a helpful writing tool: it can help you brainstorm, organize your experience, even give you a first draft. But if every candidate is using AI to write their application, it can become harder to show what makes you different. According to Amitoj Sandhu, Manager of Global Early Talent at HR platform Dayforce, employers are starting to see more applications that all sound alike. “Every single profile looks the same. They all are the same on the paper, so it becomes really hard for us to shortlist them and present in front of leaders,” he claims. Sandhu says AI is a useful starting point, but candidates need to be able to use their own voice, and  stand behind what they submit. After all, if AI is writing your resume for you, when it comes time for the interview, “will you be able to validate the results?” he says. Sandhu recommends preparing two or three strong examples from internships, school projects, or extracurricular activities that you can actually speak to authentically without farming everything out to ChatGPT. Then, be ready to walk an interviewer through those experiences and what you learned from them. With fewer entry-level roles apparently available, layering this in can make your application pop. Do use AI in your cover letter, but with caution “AI can be a great tool for writing a better cover letter. It can help candidates organize their ideas, communicate more clearly and make meaningful connections between their own interests and the company they’re applying to,” says Dan Kejsefman, Talent Director at Avature, a software development company. He says AI can raise the bar in terms of an application’s quality—but at the same time, “the motivation behind it still needs to be genuine.”  “I’d encourage candidates to start with their own reasons for wanting the job: What interests them about the company? What would they like to learn? What experiences or interests connect them to the opportunity? Then use AI to help communicate those ideas more effectively,” he says. The crucial thing is being able to explain and stand behind what’s in your cover letter. “AI can help you tell your story better,” he says, “but the story still has to be yours.” Use AI tools where you can—many jobs will expect you to use them to some extent, anyway—but standing out in an increasingly crowded entry-level field means tapping into what makes you, you. Don’t leave your curiosity at home According to Sandhu, when it comes time for the interview, curiosity is one of the biggest qualities employers look for. Missing that in an interview is “kind of a red flag for us,” Sandhu says. Sure, one way to demonstrate this is by researching the employer before the interview, and developing a genuine understanding of what the company does and the industry it operates in. But preparation is only part of it. Kejsefman says candidates also need to show genuine interest in the conversation, rather than simply relying on a list of questions prepared with AI during your interview practice. “AI can help candidates research a company, understand a role, and prepare thoughtful questions. That’s useful, and I wouldn’t discourage it,” Kejsefman explains. “But there’s a difference between asking an impressive question, and actually being interested in understanding the answer.” For example, curious candidates listen carefully, ask follow-up questions and try to understand why things work the way they do. That’s a timeless strategy, regardless of AI or not. Young workers “don’t necessarily have all the answers, and that’s perfectly fine, especially early in their careers. What matters is whether they show a real desire to learn and understand,” Kejsefman says. Do bring your own judgment to the work Sandhu says employers want candidates who can question the information AI provides, apply their own judgment and build on what the technology produces. Think of a software developer who might use ChatGPT to generate code, but still needs to determine whether it makes sense or meets the requirements or passes the right tests. Human judgment, after all, has long been touted as something that will still prove crucial in the AI era—in fact, as more decisions get outsourced to robots, it becomes even more valuable. “Can you use your own judgment to evaluate a response you get from AI? Can you build on that context? That’s what we’re looking for,” Sandhu says. In fields such as communications and journalism, employers still want to see creativity and original ideas rather than generic content generated by AI. “They want to look at how you think and what kind of ideas you can spark, not just all the generic ideas AI is producing,” Sandhu says. Kejsefman says AI adoption is still uneven across organizations, creating an opportunity for early-career professionals. A recent graduate who develops strong AI skills can bring something valuable to a team, even when working alongside people with much more professional experience. But they also bring enthusiasm and perspective older workers don’t have, and that robots definitely don’t have. Kejsefman also cautions against focusing exclusively on learning individual AI tools. As those tools continue to change, the ability to think critically, understand problems and evaluate results will become increasingly important. As AI takes on more workplace tasks, your ability to bring your own ideas, judgment and perspective to the work can help you stand out—especially when looking to break into a field or organization. Do prioritize experience over job titles Regardless of best practices, as AI continues to change the skills employers need, recent graduates may need to be more flexible about where they start their careers. For starters, Sandhu cautions against focusing too heavily on a particular job title or starting salary. “The significant mistake which they’re making is they’re running after titles and what the compensation is going to look like,” Sandhu says. Instead, he encouraged candidates to prioritize gaining experience and finding opportunities to get started, even if the position isn’t exactly what they initially envisioned or in their precisely preferred field. “Don’t run after a specific job title in the world which is changing every day,” he says. And that experience doesn’t have to come from a traditional job. Kejsefman encourages recent graduates to draw on those other past experiences, like university projects or volunteering—even personal projects or side gigs, which a lot of Gen Z already has anyway. “They need examples of situations where they’ve taken initiative, faced a problem, learned something new, or adapted when things didn’t go as expected,” Kejsefman says. “For someone starting their career, demonstrating that mindset can be much more valuable than presenting a perfectly polished result.” Make no mistake—for new workers in the workplace, it’s rough out there. But keeping these strategies, which mix time-tested tactics with AI adoption and adaptation, could open the right door at the right time.

#116508. Latest Update: Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1795 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it.
  • Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout.
  • The below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it.

Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout. After last night's driving around I would also maybe add in a quick bonus one, come to think of it: watch out for cyclists making last-minute left turns. Or don't, actually. Half of this lot deserve it….

The below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh. Though naturally I do explain the way some parts of this game work, taking away some of the sense of discovery. You can take my word for it that there's plenty more to discover beyond this though, so worry not.

If you'd like even more help navigating Leonida, then check out our wonderful guide team's GTA 6 walkthrough.

The number one thing I'd tell people to do in GTA 6 is to create lots of save files and, as you progress and start needing to overwrite them, to try to keep a roughly even spread of files through each chapter. There are various reasons for this - for one, while the game autosaves, it doesn't seem to do that successfully if you suddenly lose power to the console or witness a rare game crash, so it'll preserve your progress. More than that: GTA's story and missions are surprisingly, perhaps mysteriously reactive. Quite a lot can differ, and so being able to go back and make different choices, or play the game differently, will be something 'future you' likely appreciates.

In a recent development, in the very early game you won't have access to a bank account, but once you do: you should put every bit of cash you have in there as soon as you can. Cash is lost on death or arrest - which can happen quite often in GTA 6, funnily enough - and there's no real benefit to carrying it around. Just about everything, besides in-game strippers, can be paid for via your BuckMe account directly. And there's a relatively low $20,000 limit you really don't want to hit in the middle of raiding a gang hideout, either.

GTA 6 has a luxurious range of customisation settings, from hiding notifications about your relationship to reinstating the old 'tap to sprint' control scheme. The accessibility settings - while crucially I'm not an expert - seem considerable. And there are somewhat disguised difficult settings here around enemy damage taken and encounters with the police.

Fairly early in the game you'll gain access to the Scooter Bros. App, which lets you repair or summon your owned vehicles at will. Crucially, there's also an option to pay a one-off fee to unlock three free uses of the app per day. At $12,000, in the early game this is a lot of dosh, but once you rack up that kind of money after advancing through the game a little, it's well worth the initial cost. The sooner you unlock it, the more value it provides over time on a cost-per-use basis. And trust me when I say: as the game's intensity ramps up, you will probably find yourself needing to repair and recover your vehicles quite often. (Also, in Chapter 1, before you get access to the app, you can access the same service by going to your phone's contacts and calling Joey - handy!).

Rockstar has somewhat disincentivised it by adding a cost and putting it in your phone's apps rather than the main map screen, but you can fast travel around Leonida if you ever want or need to. This is done via the RideMe Uber-like app. It's not cheap - you'll need to pay both the fee for the journey and an additional $100 to skip that journey and instantly arrive at your destination, but in certain scenarios it might prove useful. To skip the journey, hold L2/LT once in the cab, and then hold down Triangle/Y when the option is shown. However….

While it's possible to journey-skip your way around this world, having tested that first hand I'd advise against it. It might be obvious, but GTA 6 is genuinely designed around you manually travelling around, typically in the car. If you skip all your commutes between missions or locations, you'll miss out on the game's dozens and dozens of emergent events, which lead to anything from one-off jokes to entire mission chains. The car is also, in a way, kind of the heart of the entire game. Relish the intentional slowness!

Industry observers note that again, avoiding spoilers here, but in the mid game the 'true' loop of GTA 6 gameplay will properly reveal itself, in all the many methods of earning money and the increased emphasis on doing so. You can of course play the game however you like, but having reached the end and looked back from that point, I found that if there was a particular moment to set aside as the time for aimlessly exploring the world, it was from around Chapter 3 onwards. You'll have enough tools to be able to see it at more or less its fullest then, but also won't have missed anything essential by waiting until that point to take your foot off the pedal either.

Industry observers note that A handy early-game tip here that even I missed when I was playing, but have since discovered: two islands in the small cluster of them to the south-west of Jason's early game home each house a really useful weapon, in a silenced pistol and a handy shotgun. You'll own these permanently once found, and so they can be incredibly helpful for navigating missions with maximum or minimal violence. Look for shipwrecks on those islands to find them. The pistol is hidden under a little hatch on the deck of a shipwreck on the southernmost point of the south-easternmost island. The shotgun is next to a small wooden wrecked boat around the middle of the northernmost island.

Recent findings suggest that A mechanic I slightly underused at first was the ability to 'save' a given outfit to your car. You can do this either from your car's trunk or from the wardrobe, and it's hugely useful as you start to get into more elaborate scrapes with the police (and also if you just like to role-play a bit and don the right outfit for the right occasion).

According to recent reports, there are lots of reasons for this, from the moments of intimacy it affords you with your partner, to the extra buffs you can get from resting. Sleep at home, for instance, and you can then immediately pet your snake (ahem), down a coffee or drink from the fridge, grab an apple and take a shower for a range of buffs across health, stamina, and focus. Each of these will last quite some time, so it's worth the few minutes of time to do them. Eating and drinking regularly also helps you maximise gains in the gym.

Rockstar seems to enjoy the concept of a game within a game, and that's exemplified well by the in-game phone. You can find missions via scrolling Snapmatic, it's in-game social media, or from texting various contacts you pick up as the game progresses. It's worth checking it every now and then just to see if anything interesting - or just funny or absurd - might pop up.

According to recent reports, car trunks, both those belonging to the public and the police, are often well worth a look. Even if you're quickly nabbing a car for a short-term dash, take a moment to check the boot for anything worthwhile. We've found everything from sellable narcotics to very useful weapons in there. In cop cars, that goes up several notches, too.

Industry observers note that A small thing, but in-mission checkpoints are relatively generous in GTA 6. If you really wanted to complete a mission a certain way - undetected or non-violent, say - then don't be afraid to quickly re-load rather than feeling you need to manually load up an earlier save, or give up on your goal entirely. It's also helped me out with a few minor progress-jamming bugs along the way too.

This might seem obvious, but it's worth emphasising for early-game players: it's very, very rare that you actually need to kill anybody in GTA 6. Enemies are fully incapacitated when you see a yellow hit marker over your crosshairs, even if that just comes from blasting away at their toes. If you make a habit of navigating combat this way then that also makes it much easier to recover your 'Professional' criminal status if you ever do decide to go full rampage. Though you can, of course, ultimately play this game however you like. Just be aware there may be consequences, known and unknown, as you go. Also: don't forget to click the right analog stick to aim down sights - it's an easy thing to forget when playing a third-person shooter like this, and not always the best way to operate, but incredibly helpful in select circumstances.

In a recent development, throughout the game you'll have a 'family savings' goal to hit. As you progress you'll find more ways to earn money much faster, and so it's easy to make up for lost time here if, later on, you decide that actually you do want to think about the future after all. But that grind will be a fair bit less painful if you chip away at the target as you go. As long as you save yourself some fun money - a few hundred in the early game, few thousand in the mid game, and a few tens of thousands late on - then you'll have enough to do key things like buying latest garages to register vehicles, or paying to register them themselves.

Sources indicate that throughout your time with GTA 6 you'll encounter moments when you need to make a choice. Interestingly, I noticed at least a few occasions where a scenario changed when I just waited, doing nothing at all. Sometimes that might mean a choice is made for you - so waiting is a risk - but on other occasions upcoming options become available. Sometimes they might mean a genuinely different consequence, others they might just lead to characters reacting in a certain kind of way. But it's worth experimenting - your first options aren't always your only ones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Costco is coming to the rescue of anyone scrambling to put together a last-minute Thanksgiving dinner, bringing back its affordable meal kit with enough food to feed up to eight people.

Earlier in November, Costco made headlines for selling a massive 30-pound Thanksgiving dinner for $200, complete with a turkey, numerous sides, and desserts.

However, that extravagant feast required customers to place their orders by November 13, leaving anyone who missed the deadline out of luck.

Thankfully, with just days to go until Thanksgiving, Costco has brought back a considerably cheaper alternative that doesn’t require a pre-order.

A post shared by Laura Jayne Lamb (@costcohotfinds).

As reported by Delish, Costco’s Kirkland Signature Turkey Dinner Kit has returned to the retailer’s deli department for 2026.

Each kit comes with a seasoned, boneless half turkey breast, herbed stuffing, Yukon Gold mashed potatoes, green beans, cranberry sauce, and gravy.

The kits are priced at $3.99 per pound and weigh around 10 pounds, meaning shoppers can expect to pay roughly $40 for the entire meal.

According to Costco’s official product listing, each kit serves seven to eight people, bringing the cost down to around $5 per person.

Recent findings suggest that while the turkey still needs to be cooked, much of the preparation has already been taken care of. The meat even comes sitting on top of the stuffing, allowing the juices to soak into it while roasting.

Unlike Costco’s more expensive Thanksgiving feast, however, the kit doesn’t include dinner rolls or dessert, so you might want to grab one of the retailer’s famous pumpkin pies while you’re there.

Costco isn’t the only retailer trying to make Thanksgiving more affordable. Walmart is offering a $35 feast that feeds 10 people, while Amazon has a $25 Thanksgiving meal with same-day delivery on qualifying orders.

Costco is selling a massive 30-pound Thanksgiving dinner for $200, but you have to pre-order it.

Walmart takes on Costco and Amazon with $35 Thanksgiving feast that feeds 10 people.

Amazon announces $25 “complete” Thanksgiving meal with same-day delivery.

Both of those bundles primarily consist of groceries that customers will need to prepare themselves, giving Costco an advantage for anyone looking to spend less time in the kitchen.

Just don’t leave your shopping until Thanksgiving morning, as Costco’s warehouses will be closed on November 26.

Getting asked why you haven’t bought a house this Thanksgiving? Here’s what to tell your relatives

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1015 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it’s bad enough you have to sleep on the pull-out couch for a few days, but then come the questions.
  • It’s bad enough you have to sleep on the pull-out couch for a few days, but then come the questions.
  • If the topic of homeownership—and, more pointedly, why you don’t yet own a home—comes up at Thanksgiving, here’s a stat to keep your pestering relatives at bay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’s bad enough you have to sleep on the pull-out couch for a few days, but then come the questions. If the topic of homeownership—and, more pointedly, why you don’t yet own a home—comes up at Thanksgiving, here’s a stat to keep your pestering relatives at bay. A household today earning a median income would need to save for 10.5 years to have enough for a 10% down payment on a median-priced home—that’s more than three times longer than in the 1980s, according to a new report from Realtor.com. While your relatives may bemoan the double-digit mortgage rates of the 1980s, homes on the market were relatively more affordable. That’s because the surge in home prices, and especially in recent years, has far outpaced the rise in wages, which is keeping many prospective homebuyers on the sidelines, according to the Austin-based real estate site. “The reality is that today’s aspiring buyers face a different housing market than generations before,” Hannah Jones, senior economist at Realtor.com, noted in a statement. And it’s not just that home prices have outpaced wage growth, homebuyers are also facing rising costs for insurance and homeowners association (HOA) fees that are stretching their budgets, she added. “The path to homeownership has become increasingly difficult.” In the 1980s, the median-priced home was selling for roughly 3.2 times the typical annual household income at the time, according to Realtor.com. Today, shoppers are trying to squeeze into a market where homes are selling for 4.8 times the typical household income. It’s no wonder, then, that so many younger people are living at home for longer to save up for a down payment when a first-time homebuyer is now 40 years old. WHERE HOUSING IS MORE, LESS AFFORDABLE Depending on where you live, you might already have an arsenal of mind-blowing stats about your local housing market. In some major metro areas, saving enough money for a down payment for a median-priced home has become a herculean task unto itself. People earning the median income could understandably feel locked out of the housing market in many areas. Among the 50 largest metro areas, the five where workers must save the longest for a 10% down payment on a median-priced home are:  Los Angeles, California: 24.8 years San Diego, California: 18.8 years San Jose, California: 18.4 years New York, New York: 17.0 years Boston, Massachusetts: 15.7 years On the flip side, saving up for a down payment in the following five metro areas could happen in the span of less than a decade for some households: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania: 7.2 years Detroit, Michigan: 7.6 years St. Louis, Missouri: 7.6 years Buffalo, New York: 7.9 years Cleveland, Ohio: 8.1 years Of course, housing-related costs aren’t limited to saving up for the down payment and then budgeting for monthly mortgage payments. Homeowners today must also factor in the rising costs of things like insurance or HOA fees at a time when the price of, well, everything seems to be going up. “For many younger Americans, the challenge isn’t a lack of willingness to save,” Jones said. “It’s that the financial goalposts have moved.”.

#116504. Tech Report: I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1289 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1289 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance.
  • Developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal.
  • The first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance. Voyaging uncharted waters may appear foolish to some, yet folly and heroism can often appear the same to the undiscerning eye," so states the voice of Johannes Zuch - creator, writer, director, composer, and 'perceptual architect' behind Leonida's latest favourite indie darling art game, Tenebrae Lux. It's pretentious, it's deeply up its own arse, and it's awkward and off-putting to play. A must-review for Eurogamer.

Developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal. Jason is quick to dismiss Tenebrae Lux in manufacturer, but once Cal slinks off home - hungover and dreary - I slide the disc back into my JoyStation console and sink my teeth back into it. Jason loves this stuff, really. He only keeps Time Jackers: Rewind installed so his mates don't judge him.

The first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name. It's Latin for 'darkness and light', or something similar. Is this riffing on Clair Obscur, which is French for 'light dark'? No, it's too cerebral for that - too plodding and navel-gazey. Sandfall Interactive wouldn't be this pretentious. Maybe it's a pastiche of Dear Esther, then, drawing on the tenets and schema of the 'walking simulator' genre and using that washed-out film noir aesthetic. But then, it's too wordy for that, with too many interactive and puzzle-adjacent elements. Ah, it must be mocking The Witness, instead - there's the telltale lighthouse, the 'I'm definitely not telling you where to go and what to do' internal narration, and of course the fingerprints of Johannes Zuch are all over it. Johannes Zuch, Jonathan Blow - see how they braided them together? (Sorry).

Whilst this has been created by Rockstar as a pastiche - as much loving send-up as it is withering take down - and designed to make a quick joke in the early 'Feng Shui' mission, the game is playable from start to finish if you so desire. You boot it up by inserting a physical disc, too, which is funny given the context. And it's good! Well, not good good, but it's a proper brainteaser, and ribs 2016's The Witness with such knowledge and (I think?) respect that it's hard not to be charmed by Rockstar's game-within-a-game. There are collectibles to be found that riff on Mark Z. Danielewski's House of Leaves, too, a knowing nod to the most try-hard of all try-hard literature.

Recent findings suggest that within seconds of the title screen, too, you're presented with a game-within-a-game-within-a-game. You must clear four boards filled with puzzle pieces as the protagonist mutters something mysterious and weird in his posh voice. Do so, and you unlock the door to the next location. Head up to a bunker, and you'll see a room filled with various clues - maybe it's a flashing lamp flickering in morse code, maybe it's a malfunctioning clock presenting a maths puzzle, maybe it's a pricetag on a record that changes on every visit, maybe it's a photograph with anomalous elements, maybe it's a "Developed Using Zuchworks Engine" easter egg hidden in the environment. You need to keep your wits about you, because one of these clues changes every time you enter - and the clue corresponds to a date that changes on a calendar on the wall.

You can look up a guide if you need to, or you can spend far too long figuring out how all this relates to the telephone you can find in the room on your own, like muggins here, before opening up the path to the next puzzle. Look at the image below to see the level of record-keeping and brainteasing this bizarre little game prompted from me. I will say, the sense of achievement you get from playing around with this stuff is pretty remarkable, given - let's not forget I'm actually playing Grand Theft Auto 6 whilst I'm wandering around in the black and white murk trying to complete a puzzle game for no actual reward.

In a recent development, the bunker room is, by far, the hardest part of Tenebrae Lux. From here, things ease up: you need to figure out the right sequence of glyphs on a bridge, and then put some distance between yourself and a curious and rather creepy suited man that's seemingly figuring things out ahead of you in a location inspired by, I think, The Backrooms (or Portal, or Superliminal, or maybe something else entirely. Who knows what Zuch was thinking?).

"With the last enigma finally mastered," the narrator drones in his bumbling monotone, "I step forward into the void, the shadows swallow, consuming all, and then finally the sweet embrace of darkness of which there is no end." 'You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience', Tenebrae Lux tells me, before cutting to the best joke of the whole thing: the credits roll much akin to something Hideo Kojima would produce.

Sources indicate that so, what do you get out of all of this? Well - just like real puzzle games in the real world - nothing, really. If you've not completed one of the other three fully playable games in GTA 6, you will get a trophy/achievement. But given the main game is all about Jason and Lucia's desperate scramble to escape the poverty trap, to try and break free of the cycle of debt, violence, and consequence that keeps them clinging to Leonida's seedy underbelly, there's no monetary reward. There's no 'progress' in the sense of the protagonist's shared story.

Industry observers note that even in terms of your own cold, hard, mathematical 'completion' you only need to boot each of the four games up once in order to work towards GTA 6's 100% completion. So what's the point of all this? Why did I spend the better part of 90 minutes trying to figure out how to find a sliver of light in the dark in Tenebrae Lux? The game is a wonderful pastiche in that, essentially, it's not really saying anything. You can probably project some vague meaning onto it if you wish - I'm pretty certain the protagonist literally 'finds himself' at the end - but glib little readings like that are ten-a-penny in this genre.

I think the most impressive thing about Tenebrae Lux is that it exists. You're teased with it in an early mission - Rockstar may as well say 'look, we put a game in a game, lol' - but it's more than that. This is what happens when Rockstar's 4700-plus developers are given the room to… develop. Tenebrae Lux could very easily have been a non-interactive experience, a quick, cheap joke shown over-the-shoulder taking a drive-by pop shot at Johnathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck, or any and all of the above. Or maybe it could be a 'vertical slice', an incomplete demo, a teaser. But it's not, because nothing about GTA 6 is quick or cheap.

GTA 6, in every single conceivable way, is a premium experience - part-sandbox, part-simulation, part-otherworld. To create not just one, but four fully playable and completable games within that framework is showboating, sure, but to make that game actually good and - perhaps controversially - even better than some of the games it's pastiching… Well, it's just rubbing salt in the wound, really.
